explanations.answer: It defiles His sanctuary and profanes His holy name
explanations.explanation: The LORD gives His reason in His own words: “…he has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name.” (Leviticus 20:3) The reason is right there in the verse, so we don't have to guess at one. Giving his offspring to Molech touched the LORD's sanctuary and His holy name.

explanations.answer: It breaks a promise the people made to Moses
explanations.explanation: No promise to Moses, Israel's leader, shows up in this verse. The reason the LORD gives is that “…by giving his offspring to Molech, he has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name.” (Leviticus 20:3) The LORD names two things that were touched, His sanctuary and His holy name. I'd stick with the reason He actually gives.
